Intra-articular injection of different types of blood-derived products is gaining popularity and clinical importance in the treatment of degenerative cartilage disorders such as osteoarthritis. The regenerative potential of two types of platelet-rich plasma (PRP), prepared in the presence of EDTA (EPRP) and citrate (CPRP) and an alternative blood product-hyperacute serum (hypACT) was evaluated using a 3D osteoarthritic chondrocyte pellet model by assessing the metabolic cell activity, cartilage-related gene expression and extracellular matrix deposition within the pellets. Chondrocyte viability was determined by XTT assay and it revealed no significant difference in metabolic activity of OA chondrocyte pellets after supplementation with different blood products. Nevertheless, the selection of blood products influenced the cartilage-related genes expression, ECM morphology and the tissue quality of pellets. Both PRP types had a different biological effect depending upon concentration and even though CPRP is widely used in clinics our assessment did not reveal good results in gene expression either tissue quality. HypACT supplementation resulted in superior cartilage-related genes expression together with tissue quality and seemed to be the most stable product since no remarkable changes were observed between the two different concentrations. All in all, for successful regenerative therapy, possible molecular mechanisms induced by blood-derived products should be always carefully investigated and adapted to the specific medical indications. osteoarthritic chondrocytes cartilage 3D pellet culture blood products platelet-rich plasma hyperacute serum 1. Introduction Osteoarthritis (OA) is a common form of degenerative, joint destructive disease affecting 70% of the population beyond 70, where up to 30% of the cases are symptomatic. Due to demographic changes, this number is likely to increase [ 1 , 2 ]. The underlying pathophysiology of OA is multifactorial, however, the combination of factors such as age, progressive cartilage degeneration and joint inflammation seems to be crucial to its etiology [ 3 ]. Minor cartilage injuries may heal on their own within a few weeks, but full-thickness defects have a poor capacity for repair and it may lead to OA [ 4 , 5 ]. Regenerative therapy is a novel strategy to stimulate proliferation and matrix synthesis of chondrocytes and neighbouring cells to restore a normal structure and function of damaged cartilage. Different studies have proposed the use of platelet derivatives in order to facilitate the repair system of bones and cartilages [ 6 ]. In vitro experiments showed that platelet-rich-plasma (PRP) supplementation enhances proliferation, migration and matrix biosynthesis of articular chondrocytes [ 7 ]. However, heterogeneous production protocols lead to discrepancies in PRP standardization and due to the different composition, it is difficult to predict the effects of a treatment strategy. PRP was reported to contain pro-inflammatory components such as leucocytes or fibrin [ 8 , 9 ] the presence of which might be unfavourable in the case of an inflamed joint. This demonstrates the necessity for an extensive understanding of the underlying biologic mechanisms of blood-derived products action. Hyperacute serum (hypACT) is a PRP alternative, cell- and platelet-free blood product without fibrin matrix [ 10 ]. It was shown that chondrocytes supplemented with hypACT (previously called HAS) proliferate faster even when affected by osteoarthritis. Addition of hypACT to adipose-derived stem cells cultured in 3D pellets together with chondrogenic differentiation medium resulted in obtaining pellets with good tissue quality and enhanced expression of cartilage-related genes. However, our previous studies evaluating hypACT and PRP influence on OA chondrocytes behaviour were limited to monolayer culture experiments which may not adequately mimic the in vivo conditions [ 11 , 12 , 13 ]. This study aimed to (i) evaluate and (ii) compare the effects of different blood-derived products: hypACT and two types of PRP upon their regenerative potential assessed by cell proliferation and matrix synthesis in an established 3D OA chondrocyte in-vitro culture system. 2. Materials and Methods 2.1. The Preparation of Blood Products Blood products: hypACT, leukocyte-poor PRP prepared from blood anticoagulated with EDTA (EPRP) and leukocyte-poor PRP prepared from trisodium citrate (CPRP) were produced from whole blood collected from 9 healthy donors (5 female, 4 men; age between 25 and 45 years old). During the collection around 50 mL of whole blood was drawn from each donor. The following volumes of blood were used: 16 mL for EPRP, 16 mL for CPRP and 18 mL for hypACT. Each blood product was prepared by methods described by Neubauer, Kuten et al. [ 12 ]. All nine samples of each product were pooled and immediately used for experiments or stored at −80 °C for later use. Written informed consent was obtained from all donors. 2.2. OA Chondrocytes Isolation Human osteoarthritic articular cartilage was obtained from 5 patients (3 female, 2 male) who had an average of 73 years and underwent total knee arthroplasty. Chondrocyte isolation and expansion protocols were previously described by Bauer et al. [ 13 ]. Written informed consent was obtained from all donors. Ethical approval for the use of OA chondrocytes was obtained from the Ethics Committee of Lower Austria (GS1-EK-4/480-2017).

extracted_data.document_summary: This study evaluated and compared the regenerative potential of different blood-derived products (EDTA-PRP, Citrate-PRP, and hyperacute serum [hypACT]) in a 3D osteoarthritic chondrocyte pellet model over 21 days. Key assessments included metabolic cell activity, cartilage-related gene expression (SOX9, COL2AB, COL1A1, MMP3, P21), and extracellular matrix (ECM) morphology and quality, using 1% or 5% concentrations of the products. HypACT consistently demonstrated superior and more stable results for cartilage-related gene expression and tissue quality. In contrast, Citrate-PRP showed negative effects on ECM production, chondrocyte presence, and gene expression, which was partly attributed to anticoagulants and extensive platelet accumulation. Metabolic activity generally showed no significant differences among the blood products compared to controls, though some variations were observed.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Blood-derived products: hyperacute serum (hypACT), leukocyte-poor Platelet-rich plasma prepared with EDTA (EPRP), and leukocyte-poor Platelet-rich plasma prepared with trisodium citrate (CPRP).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Blood products (hypACT, EPRP, CPRP) were prepared from whole blood (18mL for hypACT, 16mL for EPRP, 16mL for CPRP) and used as 1% or 5% (v/v) supplementation in 3D osteoarthritic chondrocyte pellet cultures for 21 days; 10% concentration was deemed unsuitable. HypACT showed stable effects across both 1% and 5% concentrations. For EPRP, 1% was favored over 5% due to better glycosaminoglycan deposition and lower platelet accumulation, with concentration influencing specific gene expressions (SOX9, MMP3, COL2AB, COL1A1). CPRP at both 1% and 5% concentrations resulted in poor tissue quality and no increase in COL2AB production, with extensive platelet accumulation observed.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: unchanged for most groups; higher for some; lower for one control group
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant changes were observed in metabolic activity compared to control (1% FCS) for most blood products (hypACT, EPRP, CPRP 1% and 5%). HypACT, EPRP, and 1% CPRP showed approximately 1.5-fold higher activity than 1% FCS, while 5% CPRP showed a slight 1.2-fold increase. 5% FCS resulted in lower metabolic activity. High metabolic activity with CPRP was noted, but potentially attributed to extensive platelet accumulation rather than true chondrocyte health.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Represents cellular energy metabolism, overall cell health, viability, and proliferation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Supplementation of 3D OA chondrocyte pellets for 21 days with 1% or 5% concentrations of EDTA-PRP (EPRP), Citrate-PRP (CPRP), hyperacute serum (hypACT), or Fetal Calf Serum (FCS) as control.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the general cell health, viability, and proliferation; discrepancy with histological and gene expression results for CPRP suggests potential confounding factors like platelet accumulation.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Extracellular matrix (ECM) morphology and Tissue quality
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Morphological assessment, histological observation, tissue quality evaluation

measured_effect.direction_of_change: improved (for hypACT); poor/lower (for EPRP and CPRP)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: HypACT supplementation consistently resulted in superior ECM morphology and tissue quality. 5% EPRP showed slightly lower ECM quality, while 1% and 5% CPRP led to poor and very poor ECM production and tissue quality.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Defines the structural integrity, biomechanical properties, and overall organization of cartilage tissue.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Supplementation of 3D OA chondrocyte pellets with hyperacute serum (hypACT), EDTA-PRP (EPRP), or Citrate-PRP (CPRP).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A direct measure of regenerative therapy efficacy and the potential for structural restoration of damaged cartilage; poor quality indicates negative effects on tissue formation.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: OA Chondrocytes (3D pellet cell culture model)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: generally higher (increased expression); lower (not significant) for some groups
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Generally higher expression in all groups compared to day 0. Significant increases observed with FCS (1% and 5%), hypACT (1% and 5%), and EPRP 1%. Lower, non-significant levels were expressed with EPRP 5%, CPRP 1%, and CPRP 5%.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A chondrogenic-related gene and transcription factor crucial for chondrocyte differentiation and cartilage formation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: 21 days of 3D pellet culture of OA chondrocytes with 1% or 5% supplementation of hypACT, EPRP, CPRP, or FCS.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher expression indicates enhanced chondrogenic differentiation and cartilage matrix production; lower (non-significant) suggests less effective chondrogenesis or impaired cartilage regeneration.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: OA Chondrocytes (3D pellet cell culture model)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: significantly higher for some groups; no increase or significantly lower for others
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher expression vs. day 0 for FCS (1% and 5%), hypACT 1%, and EPRP 1%. A non-significant trend was identified for hypACT 5%. No increase was seen with CPRP (1% and 5%), where levels were significantly lower than FCS (1% and 5%) and also lower than hypACT 1% and EPRP 1%.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A primary structural component of articular cartilage, indicative of healthy chondrogenic matrix production.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: 21 days of 3D pellet culture of OA chondrocytes with 1% or 5% supplementation of hypACT, EPRP, CPRP, or FCS.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher expression signifies better cartilage matrix synthesis and a more chondrogenic phenotype; lower expression indicates impaired cartilage formation or a less desirable phenotype associated with OA.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: OA Chondrocytes (3D pellet cell culture model)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Overall increase in expression observed in most groups, with highest values in 5% FCS and 5% hypACT. Specifically upregulated in hypACT 5% (significant vs. CPRP 1%, p=0.02) and EPRP 1% (significant vs. CPRP 1%, p=0.003). Levels in 1% EPRP were similar to 5% EPRP, 1% FCS, and 1% hypACT.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A hypertrophic differentiation marker, typically associated with fibrous tissue formation and dedifferentiated chondrocytes, rather than healthy articular cartilage.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: 21 days of 3D pellet culture of OA chondrocytes with 1% or 5% supplementation of hypACT, EPRP, CPRP, or FCS.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Upregulation indicates hypertrophic differentiation or fibrous tissue formation, generally undesirable in articular cartilage repair, suggesting a less healthy or stable cartilage phenotype.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: OA Chondrocytes (3D pellet cell culture model)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: extensive drop (lower); moderate, not significant decrease
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: High production and activity are observed during OA development. A significant drop in expression was observed with 1% EPRP supplementation (p < 0.001) vs. day 0. A moderate, non-significant decrease vs. day 0 was seen with hypACT 5% and EPRP 5%.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An enzyme involved in the degradation of extracellular matrix components, including cartilage, contributing to tissue remodeling and pathological destruction.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: OA development (general), and 21 days of 3D pellet culture of OA chondrocytes with 1% or 5% supplementation of hypACT, EPRP, CPRP, or FCS.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher levels indicate cartilage degradation and OA progression. Lower expression suggests reduced cartilage degradation and a more stable cartilage environment, which is generally beneficial for repair.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: OA Chondrocytes (3D pellet cell culture model)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher for one group; stable (unchanged) for others
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Expression was higher only in OA chondrocytes treated with 5% FCS, though this was a non-significant trend with no significant difference vs. day 0. It remained stable in all other tested groups.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A cell cycle inhibitor involved in senescence and apoptosis; its expression is often upregulated in senescent cells.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: 21 days of 3D pellet culture of OA chondrocytes with 1% or 5% supplementation of hypACT, EPRP, CPRP, or FCS.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher expression suggests increased cellular senescence, which can be linked to reduced cell viability and compromised tissue quality, detrimental to tissue regeneration.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 1% EPRP favored deposition over 5% EPRP. HypACT supplementation resulted in superior deposition.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Major components of the extracellular matrix of cartilage, providing structural support, hydration, and biomechanical properties.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: 1% and 5% EPRP, and hypACT supplementation in chondrocyte pellet culture.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher deposition indicates improved cartilage matrix production, essential for the structural integrity and functional health of cartilage.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher platelet accumulation was observed with 5% EPRP. Extensive platelet accumulation was noted with 1% and 5% CPRP, particularly after 21 days of cultivation with 5% CPRP.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A cellular component of blood products, involved in signaling, coagulation, and potentially influencing tissue response.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Supplementation of OA chondrocyte pellets with 1% and 5% EDTA-PRP (EPRP) or Citrate-PRP (CPRP).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: High accumulation might detrimentally alter forming tissue quality and explain discrepancies in metabolic activity, suggesting it is a detrimental factor for tissue quality in PRP treatments.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Diminished chondrocytes presence observed with 1% and 5% CPRP.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Primary cells responsible for cartilage formation and maintenance.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Supplementation of OA chondrocyte pellets with 1% and 5% Citrate-PRP (CPRP).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates poor chondrogenesis and a negative effect of CPRP supplementation on cellularity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Present in PRP preparations, specifically citrate in CPRP and EDTA in EPRP.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Reduce the natural coagulation cascade by chelating calcium ions (EDTA) or other mechanisms (citrate), influencing cellular environment and physiological processes.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Preparation of Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP) types, implicated in differential effects on chondrocyte behavior and tissue formation compared to hyperacute serum (hypACT) or Fetal Calf Serum (FCS).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: The presence and type of anticoagulant can significantly impact cellular responses; EDTA's chelating properties may prevent chondrogenesis inhibition, while its absence or other effects in CPRP may contribute to inferior chondrogenic outcomes.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Conceptual/Theoretical (based on known properties of PRPs)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: High, non-physiological concentration of growth factors present in PRPs.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Regulate cell growth, proliferation, differentiation, and matrix synthesis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Implied comparison of chondrocyte behavior between EPRP and CPRP vs. hypACT and FCS, where high growth factor concentrations in PRPs might contribute to observed discrepancies or negative effects.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Non-physiological concentrations of growth factors can lead to unpredictable or detrimental cellular responses, potentially explaining observed negative effects or discrepancies in PRP treatments.
